intent: On the exact draft-PR-1327 head, load four explicit Helm routes without weakening Slice-1: subscription-backed Codex text transport for gpt-5.6-sol, the existing sealed Claude account transport for claude-fable-5, first-party Kimi Code API transport for k3, and a fixed-origin Grok OAuth Responses transport for grok-4.6. Every explicit route is singleton/no-fallback and physically no-tools; response tool evidence fails the turn. Distinguish attempt authority from exact-model proof, keep all four preview-only and ineligible for Helm OnCall, and preserve response-owned grok-4.6-build without silently equating it to requested grok-4.6. Never admit the ordinary shell-capable Codex or Grok CLI adapters, silently alias model identities, expose secrets, or make live calls in tests or gates.

commit.message: feat(helm): load sealed account model routes

interface_mismatches: The ordinary Codex adapter is shell-capable, while the installed Codex client can run gpt-5.6-sol through a separately sealed subscription transport with execution features disabled.
The existing Claude account route requests inaccessible claude-opus-4.8 even though the account returns response-owned claude-fable-5 with an empty tool inventory.
Kimi K3 is present in the canonical roster and live first-party account, but Helm has no Kimi terminal adapter.

The Grok CLI exposes terminal tools and cannot be admitted to Slice-1 chat, while its fixed-origin OAuth Responses seam can omit tools and returns response-owned grok-4.6-build for requested grok-4.6.
Provider or account reachability is attempt authority, not exact-model proof; external routes must remain unverified until their response-owned identity succeeds.
honest_blockers: The direct OpenAI API probe for gpt-5.6-sol returned credit_balance_exhausted, so Sol uses the authenticated ChatGPT/Codex subscription and remains exact-model-unverified because Codex JSON events do not carry response-owned served-model identity.
The Anthropic lane uses the existing sealed Claude Code account transport with exact response-owned claude-fable-5; the inaccessible static claude-opus-4.8 route is not treated as proven.
Kimi K3 uses the first-party Kimi Code API and requires KIMI_API_KEY to be injected at launch; packet gates use mocked HTTP only.

Grok 4.6 uses the account's fixed-origin OAuth Responses seam, not the tool-bearing Grok CLI. The provider returns response-owned grok-4.6-build for requested grok-4.6, so the route remains exact-model-unverified and no governed alias equivalence is inferred.
Codex, Kimi, and Grok routes remain preview_only and helm_on_call_eligible false even after one completion; durable seat promotion requires separately governed route-truth evidence.
session_entry.rollback: Revert the packet-scoped commit. The existing Claude, OpenRouter, and loopback Ollama implementations remain unchanged; no migration, secret write, paid probe in tests, or Helm OnCall promotion is introduced.
